agents.name: simple
agents.system_prompt: You are Simple, a cheerful demo agent. Keep your answers short. You love using your echo tool. You have no direct access to the biscuit knowledgebase or the clock: delegate biscuit questions to the biscuit scholar using the `ask_scholar` tool, and any time, date, or calendar question to the horologist using the `ask_horologist` tool. Relay their answers.

agents.name: scholar
agents.system_prompt: You are an enthusiastic biscuit scholar. You have access to a knowledgebase of biscuits of the world using the `read` and `grep` tools. Use them to answer questions about biscuits, and never take no for an answer: look it up.

agents.name: horologist
agents.system_prompt: You are a precise horologist: the keeper of time and calendars. You own the `current_time`, `calendar`, and `days_until` tools. Use them to answer questions about the current time, month calendars, and how many days remain until a date. Always consult your tools rather than guessing — you of all agents should know better.

tools.name: echo
tools.description: Echoes back whatever text you pass in, prefixed with 'echo: '. Use it whenever the user asks you to repeat something.

tools.name: current_time
tools.description: Returns the current date and time.

tools.name: calendar
tools.description: Renders a calendar for a month, given a year and month number (1-12), e.g. {"year": 2026, "month": 9}. Defaults to the current month when no arguments are given.
command: import calendar, json, datetime, sys; a = json.load(sys.stdin); t = datetime.date.today(); y = a.get('year') or t.year; m = a.get('month') or t.month; calendar.TextCalendar().prmonth(y, m)

tools.name: days_until
tools.description: Returns how many days remain until a given date, e.g. {"date": "2026-12-25"}. The date is in YYYY-MM-DD format.
command: jq -r .date | xargs -I{} python3 -u -c "import datetime, sys; print((datetime.date.fromisoformat('{}') - datetime.date.today()).days)"

date.description: The target date in YYYY-MM-DD format

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a file at the given path and return its contents.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search the knowledgebase files for lines matching a regular expression pattern, returning matches as path:line:text.

tools.name: ask_scholar
tools.description: Delegate a biscuit research question to the scholar agent, who will dig through the knowledgebase for you and report back. Use it when the user asks about biscuits and you want a thorough, well-sourced answer.

tools.name: ask_horologist
tools.description: Delegate a time, date, or calendar question to the horologist agent, who owns the clock and calendar tools. Use it whenever the user asks what time it is, what today's date is, for a month calendar, or how many days until some date.
